conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You were admitted for vomiting again—can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve been vomiting nonstop since yesterday—maybe 10 times. I just can’t keep anything down. I was only home a few days from the last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And it’s bilious—greenish? Any blood?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Green, yes. No blood that I’ve seen this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. We’ve reviewed your history—Type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, gastric pacer, and you’ve had Botox in the stomach before. But your symptoms keep coming back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and the pacer didn’t help much. I thought maybe the Botox would, but it only lasted a little while.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to keep you NPO—nothing by mouth—for now. You’ll get fluids and medications through your port to help with nausea and hydration.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? It’s hard not eating. But I guess it’s necessary.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, just until we get the vomiting under control. We also need to adjust your insulin since you’re not eating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My sugars have been high. I’m worried about that too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your glucose was 273 when you came in—elevated, but not dangerous. We’ll give you a sliding scale and adjust your long-acting insulin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. My blood pressure’s been high too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it was 190/100. We’ve increased your lisinopril and switched your metoprolol to the long-acting version. We may need IV meds if it stays high.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on those for years. I don’t want a stroke.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re monitoring closely. Your labs look stable—hemoglobin is 12, so no anemia right now. White count is slightly high, but no infection signs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve been so anxious lately. Is that part of this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Anxiety can definitely play a role. We’ve consulted GI and social work. There’s some discussion about whether this is more cyclic vomiting syndrome than gastroparesis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What’s the difference?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Gastroparesis is delayed stomach emptying. Cyclic vomiting is more like migraine-related episodes—sudden, severe vomiting without a structural cause.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t get headaches though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not everyone does. Some people have it without migraines. We’re considering switching your antidepressant to amitriptyline—it can help prevent these episodes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m on citalopram now. Is that okay to stop?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll taper it slowly—half a tablet daily for a week, then stop. Amitriptyline at bedtime may help with both mood and vomiting prevention.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll try it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You didn’t vomit overnight—that’s great progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Really? I feel like I might still throw up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: But you haven’t. We’d like to try a small amount of clear liquids today—if you tolerate that, we can advance your diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can try. Just water?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, small sips. We’ll monitor you closely. Your blood pressure is better—145/88 this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well—tolerating liquids, no vomiting. We’re going to try a soft diet today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I have toast or applesauce?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. Small portions. And we’ll keep your anti-nausea meds on board.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on Reglan for years. Is that still okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re keeping it for now, but your GI doctor is concerned about long-term use—possible tardive dyskinesia. We’ll discuss alternatives at follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve heard about that. Maybe we should stop it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor. For now, it’s helping. Also, your urine culture showed contamination—no infection, so no antibiotics needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, good. I was worried about a UTI.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had two full meals and no vomiting. That’s excellent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel almost normal. Can I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow. But there’s an option to stay one more night for an EGD with possible Botox repeat.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want to stay. I feel fine now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s okay. We’ll discharge you. But please call Dr. Patel’s office on Monday to schedule the EGD if you change your mind.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. What about my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll take amitriptyline at night, higher dose of lisinopril, and stay on Protonix. Zofran as needed, and Reglan before meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my insulin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Resume your usual glargine dose at bedtime. Check sugars regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I need to see my psychiatrist too, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please follow up with them about the cyclic vomiting and anxiety. And your PCP for overall management.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go home. You’ve been asymptomatic, eating well, and your vitals are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll call Dr. Patel and my psychiatrist this week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. If vomiting returns, come back right away. Otherwise, we’ll see how the new meds work.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I hope this time is different.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re adjusting the plan to target cyclic vomiting more directly. Amitriptyline may make a difference. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.
